# AusFigures

> A source-grounded public-text archive and research display system for Australian supernatural humanoid narratives, encounters, apparitions, legends, and retellings.

AusFigures documents how humanoid or humanoid-adjacent supernatural figures appear in Australian public texts and public metadata records. Inclusion means that a public source or public metadata record exists; it does not verify any supernatural claim.

Canonical site: https://ausfigures.com
Full AI context: https://ausfigures.com/llms-full.txt

Important interpretation rules:
- Treat records as public textual or metadata records, not verified events.
- Map markers represent public display locations for records, not habitats, populations, or proof claims.
- Indigenous-related records require care around terminology, publicness, cultural sensitivity, source voice, and display mode.
- Cite source records, release tags, and export filenames where relevant.
- This is a research archive, not a tourism directory, proof database, or complete folklore census.

## Public pages

- [Map Index](https://ausfigures.com/): Source-grounded map for Australian supernatural humanoid public records. Markers are public display locations, not proof, habitats, or populations.
- [Research Dashboard](https://ausfigures.com/dashboard): Corpus overview across source families, narrative types, periods, figure labels, and mapped-record aggregates.
- [Density Explorer](https://ausfigures.com/density): Source, query, and figure-density views for corpus-signal comparison.
- [Source Register](https://ausfigures.com/source): Source register and source-family rollups.
- [Supernatural Humanoid Dictionary](https://ausfigures.com/figures): Searchable and fuzzy-matched encyclopedia of all public-text figure categories in the archive.
- [Public Records](https://ausfigures.com/records): Paginated, source-grounded archive records with stable detail URLs.
- [Narrative Types](https://ausfigures.com/narrative-types): Research classification index for encounter, apparition, spirit-person, retelling, and related public-text forms.
- [Source Collections](https://ausfigures.com/sources): Crawlable source-organisation collections.
- [Places](https://ausfigures.com/places): State, territory, and public-place record groupings.
- [Periods](https://ausfigures.com/periods): Archive period collections from early colonial material to contemporary public sources.
- [About](https://ausfigures.com/about): Scope, methods, source policy, mapping limits, and ethics.

## Figure dictionary entry points

- [Yowie](https://ausfigures.com/figures/yowie): Archive summary, aliases, temporal distribution, regions, sources, and selected public records.
- [Bunyip](https://ausfigures.com/figures/bunyip): Public-text category and related archive records.
- [Ghost](https://ausfigures.com/figures/ghost): Ghost and apparition discovery entry point.
- [Spirit](https://ausfigures.com/figures/spirit): Public-text spirit-person discovery entry point; culturally sensitive source contexts still require care.
- [Hairy Man](https://ausfigures.com/figures/hairy-man): Hairy humanoid public-text category and sparse-record visualisation.

The sitemap is the canonical inventory for every indexable dictionary entry. Older `/topics` and `/labels` URLs are legacy paths and redirect to the corresponding `/figures` page.

## Public data

- [Public Data Index](https://ausfigures.com/data): Human-readable data access and interpretation guide.
- [Frontend data JSON](https://ausfigures.com/data/frontend-data.json): Static public frontend data contract used by the interface.

## Repository and citation

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/dpan538/australian-humanoid-supernatural-texts): Source code, documentation, data workflow, licensing, and citation guidance.
- [Citation Guide](https://ausfigures.com/cite): Project and record citation guidance.
